chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, from Sadīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who has intercourse with an animal, he said:

He is to be lashed with a punishment less than the prescribed hadd, and he must pay the value of the animal to its owner because he has spoiled it for him. It is to be slaughtered, burned, and buried if it is of the kind whose meat is eaten. If it is of the kind that is ridden, he must pay its value, be lashed with a punishment less than the hadd, and take it out from the city in which he did that with it to another land where it is not known, then sell it there so that he is not disgraced by it.

key_terms.أَفْسَدَهَا عَلَيْهِ: He caused the animal to become spoiled for its owner.
key_terms.تُحْرَقُ وَتُدْفَنُ: It is to be burned and buried.
key_terms.دُونَ الْحَدِّ: A punishment less than the fixed prescribed hadd penalty.
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الْبَهِيمَةِ: The monetary value of the animal, owed as compensation.
key_terms.لَا يُعَيَّرَ بِهَا: So that he is not shamed or reproached because of it.
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: An animal whose meat is lawful/customarily eaten.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh on a man who has intercourse with an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning intercourse with an animal and distinguishes between animals eaten for meat and animals used for riding. It sets a discretionary punishment below the hadd, requires financial compensation to the owner, and orders disposal or relocation of the animal due to the corruption caused by the act.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5060 - Al-Hasan bin Mahbub narrated from Ishaq bin Jarir from Sadeer from Abu Jafar

Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) was asked about a man who engages in intercourse with an animal.
Imam (as) said: "He is to be lashed with a punishment less than the prescribed limit

and must compensate the owner for the value of the animal because he has corrupted it for him.
If it is an animal whose meat is consumed, it must be slaughtered, burned, and buried.
If it is an animal that is ridden, he must pay its value, be lashed with a punishment less than the prescribed limit, and take it out of the city where he committed the act to another land where it is not known, and sell it there so that he is not disgraced by it."
